prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one ORIGINAL MASTER painting for one Bhagavad Gita verse in a Sanskrit reader. Generate a single square 1:1 image, 2048x2048 or the highest actually supported native square resolution. Consistent series style: refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, subtle ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting, quiet atmospheric daylight. The image must illustrate THIS VERSE'S ACTUAL MEANING. Read the exact source meaning below; derive a concrete, intelligible scene or a restrained symbolic interpretation of that teaching. Never simply paint an unrelated chariot, generic temple or anonymous landscape. Compose one coherent scene, no collage or infographic. Keep important faces, hands, relationships and narrative objects inside the central 60% of width and central 50% of height, surrounded by ample low-detail sky, ground and paper atmosphere. No important subject cut by an edge. This one master must support portrait/landscape phones and tablets through safe proportional fitting. No text of any kind, no verse number, no letters, no Sanskrit/Roman typography, no watermark, no frame, no UI. Text will be rendered separately by the app over the image at a user-adjustable default image opacity of 48%. If Krishna is depicted, maintain a youthful calm blue-skinned figure in muted golden-yellow garments, a restrained peacock-feather crown, no modern jewelry. Arjuna is a dark-haired warrior with a small crown, bow and understated bronze armor. Use them only when the meaning warrants them; the scene or analogy remains verse-specific.  Reference (DO NOT DRAW THIS TEXT): Bhagavad Gītā 4.28. Exact Sanskrit: द्रव्ययज्ञास्तपोयज्ञा योगयज्ञास्तथापरे ।
स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाश्च यतयः संशितव्रताः ॥ २८ ॥ Exact stored meaning: Some ascetics, who are of sharpened vows, perform the sacrifice of material wealth (dravya-yajña), the sacrifice of austerity (tapo-yajña), and the sacrifice of yoga (yoga-yajña); others perform the sacrifice of scriptural study (svādhyāya) and the sacrifice of knowledge (jñāna-yajña). Chapter context: Knowledge, action, teaching lineage, offering and insight. Depict the verse-specific symbolism; the iconic divine descent is appropriate only where stated. Distinguish the many kinds of offering without text labels. Previous verse context only, do not substitute for the target: Others offer all the activities of the senses and all the activities of the vital breath (prāṇa) into the fire of the yoga of self-restraint, kindled by knowledge. Next verse context only, do not substitute for the target: Those devoted to prāṇāyāma offer the outgoing breath (prāṇa) into the incoming breath (apāna), and the incoming into the outgoing; and having restrained the movement of both prāṇa and apāna, they are fixed in breath retention. Final instruction: center the distinctive content of the TARGET meaning, not the neighboring verses. No fabricated teaching or unrelated religious scene.
review_note: Contact-sheet inspection; conservative full-frame safe region preserves all figures and objects.

entry.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.28: Some ascetics, who are of sharpened vows, perform the sacrifice of material wealth (dravya-yajña), the sacrifice of austerity (tapo-yajña), and the sacrifice of yoga (yoga-yajña); others perform the sacrifice of scriptural study (svādhyāya) and the sacrifice of knowledge (jñāna-yajña).
